events.summary: H1 is the strongest hypothesis and the change inventory is unusually clean (only two deploys and one config change in 7 days), but the causal chain rests on two unverified or untested links that could reorder the ranking: (a) the mechanism of H1 — that TemplateCache is unbounded/unevicted — is an explicit assumption, never verified from code/config or from a cache-size metric; and (b) the decisive discriminator between H1 (deploy-correlated, deploy-time-anchored memory growth) and H2/H3 (18:00Z Kafka-event-correlated or organic growth) is the shape of the memory sawtooth on 03-21 and 03-22, which was never retrieved. F16/F17/F13/F14 establish a genuine ~22–23h periodic sawtooth with the first OOM ~23h after dep-5402 landed, which is strong circumstantial support, but the first OOM (03-21T22:59Z) is only ~23h after the deploy, so the "third OOM" framing and the reporter's Kafka-replay theory cannot be fully excluded without the earlier-day memory curves and a check on whether cache size correlates with heap growth. H2 is already contradicted by F18 (no kafka-side replay/restart evidence) and by the mechanistic implausibility of retention reduction causing replay; H3 is contradicted by F1/F8/F14 (no pre-03-21 OOM history, so growth did not cross a limit organically); H4 is contradicted by F13/F14/F18. Those three are adequately downgraded; H1 needs the two pieces below, and the confidence cap should stay well below 0.85 until then. Scope across other services remains unverified and is worth one bounded check because it is cheap and discriminates H1 vs H4, but it is secondary.

events.summary: Round 2 substantially closed the gap I flagged. The decisive discriminator I requested — the pre-incident memory curves — is now in hand: F31/F32/F33/F34/F37 (T5) show the ~0.037%/min monotonic ramp with identical ~46–50% post-restart baselines across all three cycles, and a PRE-deploy baseline (03-20T18:00–03-21T00:25Z) that is flat ~47–50% with no climb, with the ramp appearing only after the dep-5402 window. That kills the two live alternatives: an 18:00Z Kafka-event-correlated cause (H2) and organic/capacity growth (H3) both predict a ramp either before 03-21 or anchored at 18:00Z on each day, neither of which exists. H2's Kafka-replay mechanism is further, independently contradicted by F18 (no replay/restart in kafka logs), F25/F26/F27 (kafka cpu, messages_in_per_s, under-replication all flat; no replay step after 18:00Z), and F28/F30 (the other observable Kafka consumer shows no lag spike or WARNs). H4 is contradicted by the same kafka health data plus isolated restart steps (F13/F14). H3 is contradicted by F36 (flat cpu ~25%, flat request_rate ~135/s), F14 (zero OOMs before 03-21), and the flat pre-deploy baseline. Rounds 3+ have little left to add: T4 confirmed the artifact body is not obtainable by any tool in this toolset, so the cache-vs-other-allocation mechanism question (H1 vs H5) is unanswerable by more queries, and F35 confirms no cache-size/heap-used/working-set metric exists to discriminate them. The one thing worth checking is the last unverified scope item from T6, but it only bears on H4, which is already contradicted on three independent axes, so it is not blocking. I accept H1 as the leading root cause with the mechanism (cache-vs-another-allocation, unbounded-vs-bounded) explicitly labeled unproven, and cap confidence at 0.8 — below 0.9 because the causal chain's final hop (which specific allocation grows) rests on an unfalsifiable-from-telemetry assumption, and because H5 remains a legitimate mechanism swap that no available tool can rule in or out.

critiques.summary: H1 is the strongest hypothesis and the change inventory is unusually clean (only two deploys and one config change in 7 days), but the causal chain rests on two unverified or untested links that could reorder the ranking: (a) the mechanism of H1 — that TemplateCache is unbounded/unevicted — is an explicit assumption, never verified from code/config or from a cache-size metric; and (b) the decisive discriminator between H1 (deploy-correlated, deploy-time-anchored memory growth) and H2/H3 (18:00Z Kafka-event-correlated or organic growth) is the shape of the memory sawtooth on 03-21 and 03-22, which was never retrieved. F16/F17/F13/F14 establish a genuine ~22–23h periodic sawtooth with the first OOM ~23h after dep-5402 landed, which is strong circumstantial support, but the first OOM (03-21T22:59Z) is only ~23h after the deploy, so the "third OOM" framing and the reporter's Kafka-replay theory cannot be fully excluded without the earlier-day memory curves and a check on whether cache size correlates with heap growth. H2 is already contradicted by F18 (no kafka-side replay/restart evidence) and by the mechanistic implausibility of retention reduction causing replay; H3 is contradicted by F1/F8/F14 (no pre-03-21 OOM history, so growth did not cross a limit organically); H4 is contradicted by F13/F14/F18. Those three are adequately downgraded; H1 needs the two pieces below, and the confidence cap should stay well below 0.85 until then. Scope across other services remains unverified and is worth one bounded check because it is cheap and discriminates H1 vs H4, but it is secondary.

challenges.issue: The core mechanism ('TemplateCache has no eviction/TTL/size bound') is listed as an explicit ASSUMPTION and is supported only by the deploy message text 'Add in-memory template cache'. No code review, config, cache-size metric, or entry-count evidence confirms unboundedness. Without it, H1's chain hop 'cache entries accumulate monotonically' is unverified, and an equally consistent alternative (the cache is bounded but something else — or the same deploy's other code — allocates) survives.

Temporal anchoring is weak at the first event: the first OOM (03-21T22:59Z) is ~23h after dep-5402 (03-21T00:00Z), and the ~22–23h inter-OOM gap is also consistent with an external daily driver (e.g. a daily batch/replay window) rather than cache-fill time. The memory_pct curve for 03-21 and 03-22 was never retrieved (F16 covers 03-23 only), so the sawtooth shape that would discriminate deploy-anchored leak from event-triggered growth is unconfirmed.

Correctly ranked low, but note the discriminator was never directly tested: kafka has no replay/throughput metric queried in 19:30–20:00Z and no log evidence of a replay (F18), so 'retention cut caused replay' is dismissed mainly by mechanistic implausibility and absence-of-evidence in an incomplete kafka telemetry set (no restarts, no memory_pct). This is acceptable given the mechanism argument, but the dismissal is partly argumentative rather than empirical.

Contradicted by F1/F8/F14 only indirectly: the absence of OOMs before 03-21 shows growth did not previously cross the limit, but if a memory limit had been lowered (per-service config query failed with budget_exhausted, F9 gap) organic saturation would revive. Low risk, but the config-absence claim rests on an incomplete query.

Scope question (whether other services/topic consumers show restarts or memory growth in the same windows) is genuinely unanswered — the observability task ran out of budget after probing only notification-service and kafka. H4 is contradicted by F13/F14 (no cross-service restart evidence obtained at all) and F18, but 'no evidence' here is also 'no query completed', so the dismissal is weaker than it reads.

Data quality: memory_pct is percent-of-limit only; no absolute working set or limit in bytes was obtained, so 'heap exceeds the pod limit' cannot be stated numerically, and the absence of a limit change rides on a config query that partly failed (budget_exhausted).

evidence_requests.rationale: H1's central causal hop — unbounded accumulation with no eviction — is currently an assumption, not a finding. A bounded cache would falsify H1's mechanism and elevate H3/H2; an unbounded one would verify it. Also determine whether dep-5402 shipped any other new allocation (e.g. per-message buffering) that could independently explain heap growth.

evidence_requests.question: Bounded scope check: for the windows 2026-03-21T21:00Z–2026-03-22T00:00Z, 2026-03-22T21:00Z–23:00Z, and 2026-03-23T19:00Z–20:30Z, report restarts, memory_pct, and consumer lag for any other services consuming the same Kafka topic/consumer group as notification-service (and for kafka itself: cpu_pct, messages_in_per_s, under_replicated_partitions). State clearly which services were and were not observable.
evidence_requests.rationale: H4 (shared infra fault) and H2 (replay flooding multiple consumers) predict correlated signals in other topic consumers; H1 predicts notification-service isolation. Remaining scope evidence was never collected because the prior observability task hit budget after probing only notification-service and kafka.

critiques.summary: Round 2 substantially closed the gap I flagged. The decisive discriminator I requested — the pre-incident memory curves — is now in hand: F31/F32/F33/F34/F37 (T5) show the ~0.037%/min monotonic ramp with identical ~46–50% post-restart baselines across all three cycles, and a PRE-deploy baseline (03-20T18:00–03-21T00:25Z) that is flat ~47–50% with no climb, with the ramp appearing only after the dep-5402 window. That kills the two live alternatives: an 18:00Z Kafka-event-correlated cause (H2) and organic/capacity growth (H3) both predict a ramp either before 03-21 or anchored at 18:00Z on each day, neither of which exists. H2's Kafka-replay mechanism is further, independently contradicted by F18 (no replay/restart in kafka logs), F25/F26/F27 (kafka cpu, messages_in_per_s, under-replication all flat; no replay step after 18:00Z), and F28/F30 (the other observable Kafka consumer shows no lag spike or WARNs). H4 is contradicted by the same kafka health data plus isolated restart steps (F13/F14). H3 is contradicted by F36 (flat cpu ~25%, flat request_rate ~135/s), F14 (zero OOMs before 03-21), and the flat pre-deploy baseline. Rounds 3+ have little left to add: T4 confirmed the artifact body is not obtainable by any tool in this toolset, so the cache-vs-other-allocation mechanism question (H1 vs H5) is unanswerable by more queries, and F35 confirms no cache-size/heap-used/working-set metric exists to discriminate them. The one thing worth checking is the last unverified scope item from T6, but it only bears on H4, which is already contradicted on three independent axes, so it is not blocking. I accept H1 as the leading root cause with the mechanism (cache-vs-another-allocation, unbounded-vs-bounded) explicitly labeled unproven, and cap confidence at 0.8 — below 0.9 because the causal chain's final hop (which specific allocation grows) rests on an unfalsifiable-from-telemetry assumption, and because H5 remains a legitimate mechanism swap that no available tool can rule in or out.

challenges.issue: The mechanism is unverified and unfalsifiable with available tooling: F20/F21 confirm the dep-5402 record exposes no eviction/TTL/size parameter and no tool returns the artifact body, and F35 confirms no cache-size/heap-used/working-set metric exists. So 'the growth is specifically the TemplateCache' and 'the cache lacks eviction' are stated as assumptions, not findings. This is acknowledged in the hypothesis text but means H1's *category* (bad_deployment dep-5402) is proven while its *stated mechanism* is not. Do not report the unbounded-ConcurrentHashMap claim as a finding.

H1 cites F36 as supporting evidence, but F36 is marked UNVERIFIED (flagged by the automated check). F36 is a load-flatness claim used to exclude H3; it is corroborated in shape by the verified F31/F32/F34 deploy-anchoring and by F14's zero pre-03-21 OOMs, so the exclusion of H3 still stands, but the flat-load evidence itself should be treated as corroborating-not-confirming.

The final hop 'heap exceeds the pod memory limit' is supported only by memory_pct percentages; no byte-level limit is exposed (F16, gaps). The three cycles reliably OOMKill at ~98%, which is strong behavioral confirmation that a fixed ceiling is hit, but the numeric limit is unverified. Minor because the kill events themselves (F13, exit 137) independently establish a ceiling was reached.

H5 is not excluded and cannot be excluded by any available query: no cache metric (F35) and no artifact body (F20) exist to separate a bounded-cache-with-retained-values or a different per-render allocation from an unbounded cache. It is correctly ranked second, but it shares H1's trigger and only differs in mechanism, so the top-of-ranking conclusion (dep-5402 is causal) is robust even though the mechanism attribution between H1 and H5 is not.

The reporter's Kafka-replay theory rests on a mechanistically implausible hop (reducing retention deletes data; it does not replay it) that H2 itself concedes as ASSUMED, and is now contradicted by F18 (no kafka replay/restart logs), F25/F26/F27 (flat kafka cpu/messages/under-replication) and F28/F30. Adequately downgraded; no further testing needed.

Cross-service scope was only partially resolved (T6 could not enumerate all consumers of the same topic/consumer group; settlement-service restarts/memory_pct and auth-service were unqueried). This is a genuine gap, but it only bears on H4, which is already contradicted by kafka-side health (F25/F26/F27), isolated restart steps (F13/F14), and the deploy-anchored sawtooth (F33/F34). Not blocking.
